slides.heading: All Kinds Of Node Depths
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve All Kinds Of Node Depths, a very hard binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Sum, over every node, of the depths of all nodes in its subtree (relative to it).
Per subtree: sumDepths = sumDepths(l) + size(l) + sumDepths(r) + size(r).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Sum, over every node, of the depths of all nodes in its subtree (relative to it). Per subtree: sumDepths equals sumDepths(l) plus size(l) plus sumDepths(r) plus size(r).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each subtree's depth sum follows from its children's: their sums plus their sizes.
slides.narration: Each subtree's depth sum follows from its children's: their sums plus their sizes.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Post-order returns size, depth sum and total
2. Depth sum equals children's sums plus their sizes
slides.narration: Step by step. First, post-order returns size, depth sum and total. Second, depth sum equals children's sums plus their sizes. Third, add everyone's depth sums.
